subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Bessemer Process: Steel for the Masses
description: A 60-second lesson on The Bessemer Process: Steel for the Masses.

hook.text: Before 1856, steel cost $300 per ton. Only swords and springs used it. Iron was king.

buildup.text: Henry Bessemer blew air through molten iron. Oxygen burned away carbon impurities in minutes.

discovery.text: The process dropped steel prices to $30 per ton. Suddenly, you could build entire buildings from it.

twist.text: William Kelly in Kentucky had the same idea first. Bessemer got the patent. Kelly got forgotten.

climax.text: Cheap steel made skyscrapers, railroads, and bridges possible. The modern world is built on Bessemer's idea.

punchline.text: Blow air through iron. Get the modern world.

quiz.question: What did the Bessemer Process do to the price of steel?
options: It doubled the price but improved quality tenfold
It dropped the price from $300 to about $30 per ton
It had no effect on price, only on production speed
